newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Mexico sees Mercosur link next year.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees Mercosur link next year.

text.p: Mexico plans to link up with the four-nation Latin American customs union Mercosur next year, a top official said Wednesday.

"We are looking for the deepest and most ambitious agreement possible," Deputy Trade Minister Jaime Zabludovsky told reporters at a conference to discuss the proposed hemisphere-wide Americas Free Trade Area (AFTA).
"We hope it will take affect in 1998."

He noted that Mexico already had individual trade pacts with the four Mercosur members -- Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. "Now we are looking at how to turn these four accords into one," Zabludovsky said.

Mexico's push for an agreement with Mercosur is shared by other countriesm and experts at the conference said wider membership in the customs union may serve as a stepping stone to the AFTA zone stretching from Alaska to Argentina.
On Tuesday, Canadian officials in Costa Rica presented Mercosur members with a proposal to join as an associate member, similar to Chile and Bolivia's relationship with the four-nation bloc.
Mexico's Zabludovsky did not say what kind of deal Mexico wanted, but Mercosur said in June it wanted a similar trade deal with Mexico as the one it signed with Chile.
Mexico is already a member of the North American Free Trade Agreement with the United States and Canada.
